L119:   * cite84†U.S. Antarctic Program L120: NSF McMurdo Station is the largest of the U.S. year-round stations and the largest station on the continent. It is the central logistical hub for the U.S. Antarctic Program (USAP), supporting research on the continent and at NSF Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station.
L121: ## cite85†Image On this page
L122: 
L123:   1. cite86†Location L124:   2. cite87†Biodiversity, natural environment and climate L125:   3. cite88†History L126:   4. cite89†Facilities L127:   5. cite90†Population L128:   6. cite91†Scientific research and activities L129:   7. cite92†Additional resources L130: ## Location
L131: 
L132:   * Situated at 77° 50.89’ S, 166° 40.11’ E on the volcanic rock of Hut Point Peninsula, Ross Island.
L133:   * The southernmost point accessible by ship.
L134:   * Located 25 miles from Mount Erebus, the world’s southernmost active volcano.
L135:   * Close to cite93†Antarctic Specially Protected Area (ASPA)†www.ats.aq 122, Arrival Heights.
L136: 
L137: cite94†Image: Clustered buildings in the snow at the base of a hill.†nsf-gov-resources.nsf.gov L138: ## Biodiversity, natural environment and climate
L139: 
L140:   * McMurdo Station is a coastal station surrounded by annual sea ice for most of the year.
L141:   * Regular wildlife sightings include penguins, seals and skuas.
L142:   * Annual mean temperature is -18°C (-0.4°F) with recorded lows of -50°C (-58°F) and highs of +8°C (46.4°F.)
L143:   * Snow accumulation can reach up to 1.5 meters annually. The station is typically snow-free in summer.
L144: 
L145: cite95†Image: Young Weddell seal in Antarctica†nsf-gov-resources.nsf.gov L146: ## History
L147: 
L148:   * The station was established on December 18, 1955, and opened in 1956 as part of Operation Deep Freeze.
L149:   * Named after its geographic location on McMurdo Sound, which is named after Lieutenant Archibald McMurdo, a Scottish naval officer and polar explorer.
L150:   * Served as the center of U.S. logistical operations during the International Geophysical Year, an international scientific effort that lasted from July 1, 1957, to December 31, 1958.
L151: cite96†Image: Men at Little America IV, saluting the U.S. flag.†nsf-gov-resources.nsf.gov L152: ## Facilities
L153:   * Functions as the primary logistics hub for the U.S. Antarctic Program.
L154:   * Infrastructure includes approximately 146 buildings of varying sizes, including:
L155:     * Repair facilities, dormitories, offices, firehouse, power plant, water plant and satellite communications.
L156:     * Recreational facilities including a library, coffee house, clubs, store and gymnasiums.
L157:     * The A. P. Crary Science and Engineering Center for scientific research, including laboratories and saltwater aquarium.
L158:   * Features a harbor, two airfields and helicopter pads.
L159:   * Linked by above-ground utility lines for water, sewer, telephone and power.
L160: cite97†Image: Scientists discuss their work in the NSF McMurdo Station's Crary Laboratory aquarium.†nsf-gov-resources.nsf.gov L161: ## Population
L162: 
L163:   * Up to 1,100 people during a week in the summer season.
L164:   * Up to 200 people during a week in the winter season.
L165:   * 2,300 people move through the station annually.
L166:   * 147,956 meals are served a year.
L167: 
L168: cite98†Image: USAP personnel arrive at NSF McMurdo Station.†nsf-gov-resources.nsf.gov L169: ## Scientific research and activities
L170:   * Close to significant research areas, including the McMurdo Dry Valleys, Mount Erebus, Cape Crozier and Cape Royds.
L171:   * Research spans various disciplines, including:
L172:     * Aeronomy and astrophysics.
L173:     * Biology and ecosystems.
L174:     * Geology, geophysics, glaciology and geomorphology.
L175:     * Ocean and climate systems, as well as ice core studies.
L176:   * The station also supports participants of the cite99†Polar STEAM†polarsteam.info program who conduct projects near McMurdo.
L177: cite100†Image: Earth scientist Jennifer Lamp adjusts some of the acoustic monitoring equipment she set up in Beacon Valley.†nsf-gov-resources.nsf.gov L178: ## Additional resources
